newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BAYERN CLINCH RECORD 14TH GERMAN CHAMPIONSHIP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAYERN CLINCH RECORD 14TH GERMAN CHAMPIONSHIP.

text.p: Bayern Munich clinched a record 14th German soccer championship on Saturday when they beat VfB Stuttgart 4-2 on the penultimate day of the season.

Two first-half headed goals from Christian Ziege and Mehmet Scholl and second-half strikes from Italian striker Ruggiero Rizzitelli and forward Marcel Witeczek secured the Bavarians an unassailable four-point lead over Bayer Leverkusen.
Leverkusen's hopes of pushing the tense title race to next Saturday's final day of the season faded in a crushing 4-0 defeat at Cologne.

Bayern have won the Bundesliga 13 times since German league football began in 1963. Their other championship came in 1932 when the title was decided after a final. But the Bavarians had to work hard for their first championship since 1994.
Stuttgart took the early initiative in the tense local derby by taking the lead with a 17th-minute goal from midfielder Danny Schwarz.
But three minutes later Ziege, playing his last home game before he joins AC Milan at the end of the season, equalised with a header from close range.
VfB's hopes of stopping Bayern winning the title then suffered a major setback in the 23rd minute when their Bulgarian international Krasimir Balakov was sent off for complaining at the referee.

Another header from close range from Scholl on the stroke of halftime gave the Bavarians a 2-1 lead at the break. With news coming through from Cologne that Leverkusen were 2-0 down at halftime, Bayern knew that the title was there for the taking.
German international Fredi Bobic equalised for Stuttgart in the 51st minute. But in the 65th minute, Rizzitelli, who has often struggled to make an impact in Munich, put Bayern ahead again.
Witeczek then struck a brilliant shot from 25 metres to seal the win and set off wild celebrations in Munich's Olympic stadium.
